cards.text: Friend, Joshua 12 is a roll call of the kings the Israelites struck down and whose lands they took. I spent years in a junk drawer counting dust, so believe me, I was BORN for a list. We start east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley all the way up to Mount Hermon.

Two kings held that side. Sihon king of the Amorites lived in Heshbon and ruled from the Arnon Valley up to the Jabbok River. And Og king of Bashan, "one of the remnant of the Rephaim…", ruled Mount Hermon, all of Bashan and half of Gilead, right up to Sihon's border. Now THAT is an introduction, friend, and the only introduction I ever got was the 25-cent price sticker on me in a closing bakery's bin!

cards.question: Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the Israelites struck down Sihon and Og. So what does Moses do with all their land?

answers.text: He gives it to some of the tribes as an inheritance
He holds it for himself as Israel's leader
He sets it aside until the war is over

cards.text: Now we cross to the west side of the Jordan, where Joshua, Israel's leader, and the Israelites conquered the kings from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak. That's hill country, foothills, the Arabah, slopes, wilderness and the Negev, the lands of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

cards.question: Joshua and the Israelites conquered the kings west of the Jordan. True or false: Joshua keeps that land under his own rule.

cards.text: Then comes the roll call, and every king gets the same little tag: the king of Jericho, one, the king of Ai, one, then Jerusalem, Hebron, Lachish, Hazor, all the way down to the king of Tirzah, one. ONE. ONE. ONE. It's like an oven timer that will NOT stop dinging! "So there were thirty-one kings in all."
